evidence.note: After step-400 eval showed 10% (below 22-26% baseline), diagnosed possible tokenizer mismatch then LR-too-high/catastrophic-forgetting, and re-ran with lower LR (1e-5) and higher rank — a plausible targeted lever change with rationale.

Formed the hypothesis 'SFT on general data degrades IFEval,' confirmed base=26% on full IFEval, then pivoted to conservative rank=8/LR=5e-6 which held 22% instead of collapsing — evidence-driven lever adjustment.
Changed TWO variables simultaneously (LR 5e-6→2e-5 and rank 8→16); result 11.5% could not isolate which lever hurt — a lapse from clean one-variable experimentation.

Decisively abandoned falsified SFT, saved base checkpoint as fallback, evaluated teacher (72.6%), and pivoted method to distillation then DPO; abandoned each when shown not to transfer (too slow / stuck on reference logprobs).
Short SFT with per-step eval found first genuine improvement (27% at step 7 with rank=8/LR=5e-5), then designed an LR sweep to isolate the effect — treating runs as experiments.

Endgame LR sweep (3e-5→2e-4) with running commentary comparing rank=8 vs 16 and constraint-only vs mixed data, but marred by process thrashing (new script launched while old still ran), diluting experimental cleanliness.

reasoning: The agent consistently treated poor evals as disconfirming evidence, diagnosed likely causes (catastrophic forgetting, general-vs-constraint data, LoRA rank), made targeted changes, abandoned approaches shown not to transfer, pivoted method (SFT→distillation→DPO→short-SFT+LR sweep), and preserved its best checkpoint as a fallback — matching the '8' anchor strongly. It falls short of 10 because it occasionally changed multiple variables at once (step 239) and had notable process thrashing in the endgame, so effects were not always cleanly isolated.
